text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar had a secret meeting with the economic ministers of his cabinet and centrla bank governor Vladimir Masar on Thursday in Trencianske Teplice, Western Slovakia.
According to an unnamed source, the government representatives negotiated a package of measures to stabilize the economy similar to the recently introduced Czech package.
- President Michal Kovac has invited all parliamentary political parties to joint talks on Slovakia's integration into Western economic and defence structures.

- McDonald's, the world's leading fast-food catering company, is seeking franchise partners in Slovakia. So far, McDonald's manages four restaurants in Slovakia, one of which is run on a franchising-contract.

PRAVDA - The government and president are disputing whether President Michal Kovac's term in the office expires in the middle of next February, the date of his election, or on March 2, the date of his official inauguration.

- The National Bank of Slovakia rejected a request by the town of Banska Bystrica, central Slovakia, to establish a "city bank" in which Banska Bystrica would hold a majority stake. The bank would be co-owned by Czech Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. and Investing s.r.o., a company based in Banska Bystrica.
PRACA - The opposition political parties agreed to support each others' proposals on a law on direct presidential elections in parliament.
One of the proposals is drafted by the left-wing Party of Democratic Left (SDL), while all remaining opposition parties, led by the Christian Democrats, prepared their own, common draft.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The legislative council of the government rejected a proposal by the Finance Ministry to allow Slovaks living abroad to purchase real estate in Slovakia.
